domain_restrictions: A must be a commutative ring.
m and n are finite lengths of the sequence; the statement does not specify whether they may be zero, but the standard reading allows empty sequences.

The phrase regular sequence carries the usual commutative algebra meaning: each element is a nonzerodivisor modulo the ideal generated by the earlier ones, and the generated ideal is proper at each stage.
The quotient is by the ideal generated by u_1 through u_m.
In the graded case, A must carry a grading compatible with the notion of homogeneous elements.
Homogeneous means each u_i and v_j lies entirely in one graded piece.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: A regular sequence in a commutative ring remains regular after passing to the quotient by the ideal generated by an initial block of the sequence. If the ring is graded and the elements are homogeneous, then their images in the quotient stay homogeneous with the same degrees.
quantifier_order: For every nonnegative integers m and n.
For every sequence u_1 through u_m and v_1 through v_n in A such that the concatenated sequence is regular.
Then in the quotient ring B equal to A modulo the ideal generated by u_1 through u_m, the images bar_v_1 through bar_v_n form a regular sequence.
If A is graded and every u_i and v_j is homogeneous, then each bar_v_j is homogeneous and has the same degree as v_j.

variables.domain: A for i from 1 to m
variables.name: u_i

witness_dependencies: Regularity of bar_v_j in the quotient depends on the earlier images bar_v_1 through bar_v_{j-1} in the quotient ring.
The degree statement depends only on the quotient map preserving the grading of homogeneous elements.

statement_nl: Let A be a commutative ring, and let u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_n be a regular sequence in A. Then the images of v_1,...,v_n in the quotient ring A/(u_1,...,u_m) form a regular sequence. If A is graded and all u_i and v_j are homogeneous, then the quotient images are homogeneous and keep the same degrees.
